Hot flashes and vaginal dryness are some of the most common symptoms of menopause and are caused by the decline in estrogen levels when women do not ovulate. Scientists have known that the levels of testosterone also decline during menopause and some have suggested that it too could contribute to menopause-related symptoms. Q: An initial public offering (IPO) is when a company sells shares of itself to the public for the first time. This means that instead of being privately owned, the company will be partly owned by the public. The company can then use the money it raises to invest in new projects, pay off debt, and fund its business operations. When a company goes public, it typically files a prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). This document provides information about the company, its financial performance, and the shares being sold. After the SEC approves the prospectus, the company can begin marketing the IPO to potential investors. During this process, underwriters are typically hired to help sell the shares to the public. Once the shares are sold, the company can begin trading on a stock exchange, such as the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) or the NASDAQ. Going public can be a significant milestone for a company, as it allows it to raise capital and increase its visibility.
